Package com.bilt.pos.nexo.client

Interface TerminalClient

All Known Implementing Classes:
BiltNexoTerminalClient
public interface TerminalClient
The transport a session uses to reach a Bilt terminal: one Nexo Sale to POI request in, one response out.

This is the whole seam between the session layer (com.bilt.pos.session) and the wire. Everything a session sends — the session bracket, loyalty, prompts, payments, display updates, aborts — goes through request(NexoTerminalAPI) or its timeout-overriding twin, and the session never asks the transport for anything else. The Nexo MessageHeader already carries POIID and SaleID on every message, so a transport is not bound to a session or a terminal: the same instance can serve many sessions addressing many devices, and an implementation needs no per-session configuration.

BiltNexoTerminalClient is the local-network implementation, speaking HTTPS to the device's own endpoint. A cloud-relayed implementation, reaching the terminal through Bilt's backend instead of the store LAN, is planned; registers that only need the session API should program against this interface so the transport can be swapped without touching checkout code.

Threading. Implementations must be safe to call from more than one thread at a time. A session issues its ordered operations from a single operation thread, but abort() and updateInputDisplay() are deliberately unordered — they exist to overlap the request currently blocking that thread — so an implementation must tolerate two concurrent requests in flight, one of them referencing the other by ServiceID. Each call blocks until the terminal answers or the timeout elapses.

  • Method Details

    • request

      com.bilt.pos.nexo.model.NexoTerminalAPI request(com.bilt.pos.nexo.model.NexoTerminalAPI request) throws BiltNexoClientException
      Sends a Sale to POI request and returns the terminal's response envelope, or null when the terminal replies with an empty body (as it does for abort requests). The request envelope must carry a SaleToPOIRequest. A BiltNexoClientException reports any transport failure; a transport timeout should surface with a SocketTimeoutException or InterruptedIOException in its cause chain so the session can classify it as such.
      Throws:
      BiltNexoClientException

    • request

      com.bilt.pos.nexo.model.NexoTerminalAPI request(com.bilt.pos.nexo.model.NexoTerminalAPI request, Duration timeout) throws BiltNexoClientException
      Like request(NexoTerminalAPI) with a per-request read timeout overriding the transport's default; null means the default. Sessions use this for operations that legitimately wait on the customer, such as prompts and card presentment.
      Throws:
      BiltNexoClientException
